findings.claim: When the formatted type already carries MessagePack contract attributes, the new collector ignores them unless a surrogate is explicitly supplied: it always builds an alphabetical, string-keyed contractless member list. A formatter requested for an existing [MessagePackObject] type with integer [Key] values, ignored members, or custom member formatters therefore produces a different wire contract instead of honoring those attributes.

receipt_plan.detail: Define [MessagePackObject] public class Sample { [Key(2)] public int A {get;set;} [Key(0)] public int B {get;set;} [IgnoreMember] public int C {get;set;} }, then generate [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class SampleFormatter : IMessagePackFormatter<Sample>. Serialize new Sample { A=1, B=2, C=3 } with the head-generated formatter and compare against the bytes from the ordinary generated formatter for the same attributed Sample; head currently emits string keys A/B (and includes C) instead of the attributed integer-key representation.
